title: Adaptive column prioritization ribbon and progressive cell hydration for Deep List view
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Introduce an adaptive column prioritization ribbon and progressive cell hydration pattern to improve perceived performance and usability for very wide virtualized tables (Deep List view). This ticket scopes the design work: interaction model for an affixed prioritization ribbon, column autoshrink rules, per-column density hint UI, and guidance for progressive hydration of expensive cell renderers when scrolling or resizing. The goal is to reduce cognitive load when many low-priority columns are present, keep keyboard and screen-reader navigation predictable, and provide clear defaults for engineering to implement batching/hydration strategies.
acceptance_criteria: Design spec with annotated states for ribbon collapsed/expanded/overflow must exist and be reviewed by Eng and PM
Component token updates (spacing & density tokens) documented and mapped to Responsive Density presets
Interaction spec for autoshrink: rules for min-width, priority-based collapse order, and animation timelines
Progressive hydration API surface described (cell placeholder states, lazy-mount cues, prefetch heuristics) and linked to a runtime ticket
Accessibility checklist satisfied: focus order preserved, ARIA announcements for column collapse/restore, keyboard affordances for ribbon control
Prototype usability test (n=6) shows majority of participants can find critical columns within 3 interactions and rate perceived performance >= 4/5
notes: Motivation: customers building analytics and inventory UIs hit poor perceived performance and lost context when tables had >20 columns. Engineering proposes either expensive synchronous renders or aggressive virtualization that breaks user mental model.
Trade-offs: ribbon approach trades a small persistent UI footprint for immediate discoverability of collapsed columns vs. context menus that hide discoverability.
Design constraints: must work with existing virtualized row renderer (RowPool V2), not add >8KB to initial bundle, and align with density tokens introduced in token-refactor-2025.
Engineering input 2026-02-24: progressive hydration feasible via row-level render queue; KV cache and batching can be reused for cell prefetch triggers.
Accessibility note from QA 2026-03-03: screen reader will need explicit live-region updates when columns auto-collapse due to resize — include role=log warnings in spec.
